_doc: What happens where two words meet. Keyed by ISO 639-3, read by
typology.sandhi_for(), applied by linearize.Sandhi at every boundary the
engine composes.
Two tables per language, because there are two processes:
elide     one word -> what it becomes before ANY vowel-initial word.
French le/la -> l'. Phonologically conditioned.
contract  a NAMED PAIR -> the single word it is written as.
Spanish 'de el' -> 'del'. Not phonological at all: it is the
identity of both words, so no vowel test would find it.
Contraction is checked first, being the more specific statement.
Only OBLIGATORY changes belong here. Optional ones are omitted: Italian
'di' -> "d'" is idiomatic in fixed collocations and merely permitted
elsewhere, so printing 'di ogni' is correct while "d'ogni" may not be.
Languages absent from this file do nothing at word boundaries, which is
most of them. Spanish has contraction but no elision: its 'el agua' is a
feminine noun taking the masculine article before stressed /a/, a
different rule in a different part of the grammar, and modelling it as
elision would wrongly catch 'la avenida' too.
A value ending in a space stays a separate word: French 'ce' -> 'cet ' is
suppletion rather than elision, but the environment is identical and this
table expresses it.
Deliberately NOT included, because the environment is narrower than the
mechanism can state: French 'si' -> "s'", which happens before 'il(s)'
but not 'elle'; and French 'ce' -> "c'", which happens only before a
form of 'etre'. Catalan 'la' keeps its vowel before unstressed i- and u-
(la universitat) and the lexicon records no stress, so the common case is
taken and that exception is knowingly missed.
